intents.name: Cache Locality and Data Reuse
intents.description: Restructure the iteration space and data movement to keep working sets within L1/L2 cache, maximizing data reuse across the compute-intensive reduction loops.
intents.rationale: The 7-dimensional loop nest with reduction over input channels and kernel spatial dimensions creates extensive data reuse opportunities. For f64 tensors with batch sizes of 128-256 and channel counts up to 512, untiled execution causes severe cache capacity misses. Tiling, interchange, promotion, and packing collectively ensure operand data is fetched once into fast cache and reused across many FMA operations.

transformations.name: Tiling
transformations.description: Partition the iteration space into multi-dimensional blocks so that the working set of each tile fits within a target cache level (L1 or L2).
transformations.rationale: Tiling is the foundational transformation for this deep loop nest. It converts a single sweep over 7 dimensions into repeated small block computations whose operand slices fit in cache, dramatically reducing main-memory traffic. The high dimensionality (4 parallel + 3 reduction) provides many tiling axes to tune for optimal cache utilization.
transformations.action_template: Tiling(tile_sizes) — tile_sizes is a vector of integers with one entry per loop dimension; a value of 0 means 'do not tile that dimension'. Partitions the iteration space into rectangular blocks. OR Tiling(loop_band, tile_sizes) — explicitly specifies which loop band to tile.

transformations.name: Loop Interchange
transformations.description: Reorder loops within a loop band to improve memory access stride patterns and maximize temporal/spatial locality for the innermost loop body.
transformations.rationale: The default loop ordering of the 7-dimensional nest may cause strided access on one or more operands due to the NCHW/FCHW memory layouts. Interchange can place loops to ensure stride-1 access on the innermost dimension and maximize reuse of loaded cache lines across adjacent iterations. The positioning of the reduction loops relative to the parallel loops is particularly impactful.
transformations.action_template: LoopInterchange(loop_band, permutation) — permutation is a reordering of loop indices within the specified loop band. OR LoopInterchangeSwap(adjacent_pair) — swap two adjacent loops in the nest.

transformations.name: Promotion
transformations.description: Copy tiled operand slices into contiguous local buffers to eliminate strided access and TLB pressure within the inner tile computation.
transformations.rationale: After tiling, operand sub-tiles may still be accessed with non-unit stride from the original tensor layout. Promotion copies these slices into compact, contiguous scratch buffers, enabling stride-1 vector loads and reducing TLB misses. This is especially impactful for the filter operand in FCHW layout where accessing a channel slice requires gathering non-contiguous memory.
transformations.action_template: Promotion(operands_to_promote) — operands_to_promote is a list of operand indices (e.g., [0], [1], [0,1,2]) specifying which operands to copy into contiguous local buffers. Promotion requires buffer (memref) form, so this action must include an internal bufferization preprocessing step.

transformations.name: Packing
transformations.description: Reorganize operand data layout into blocked/panel format so that tile-sized sub-tensors are stored contiguously in memory.
transformations.rationale: Packing transforms the global memory layout of operands to match the tiling structure, ensuring that consecutive cache lines within a tile are logically contiguous. This eliminates conflict misses and enables hardware prefetchers to work effectively. For the multi-dimensional tensor layouts in this workload, packing can substantially reduce the gap between logical tile access and physical memory layout.
transformations.action_template: Packing(packed_sizes) — packed_sizes specifies the block dimensions for the packed layout. OR Packing(operand_id, inner_perm) — specifies which operand to pack and optionally an inner dimension permutation for the packed blocks.

intents.name: SIMD and Instruction-Level Parallelism
intents.description: Exploit AVX2 vector units and instruction-level parallelism to maximize FMA throughput on the innermost computation.
intents.rationale: The target CPU achieves peak f64 throughput only when AVX2 FMA units are fully utilized. Without vectorization, only scalar FMA is used — 1/4 of peak. Vectorization maps the innermost loop iterations to SIMD lanes. Unrolling further exposes independent operations to hide FMA latency and saturate execution ports.

transformations.name: Vectorization (Sequential Tiling Preprocessing)
transformations.description: Lower the innermost loop(s) to SIMD vector operations, using sequential tiling (tile_using_for) as preprocessing to ensure loop bounds match the target vector width.
transformations.rationale: Vectorization converts scalar loop iterations into parallel SIMD operations across AVX2 lanes (4 for f64). Sequential tiling preprocessing partitions the loop into chunks of vector_width iterations, making each chunk directly mappable to a vector instruction. The outer tiles remain sequential, suitable when parallelism is handled by a separate action.
transformations.action_template: VectorizationSequential(vector_sizes) — vector_sizes specifies the SIMD width per loop dimension. Preprocessing tiles the target loops sequentially (tile_using_for) to match vector_sizes, then applies vectorization to the inner tiled loops.

transformations.name: Vectorization (Parallel Tiling Preprocessing)
transformations.description: Lower the innermost loop(s) to SIMD vector operations, using parallel tiling (tile_using_forall) as preprocessing which simultaneously distributes outer tiles across threads.
transformations.rationale: This variant combines vectorization preprocessing with thread-level parallelism in a single action. The outer tiles from preprocessing are distributed across threads via forall, while the inner tiles are vectorized. This is more aggressive than the sequential variant and may yield higher throughput when both SIMD and thread parallelism are desired from one action.
transformations.action_template: VectorizationParallel(vector_sizes) — vector_sizes specifies the SIMD width per loop dimension. Preprocessing tiles the target loops in parallel (tile_using_forall) to match vector_sizes and distributes outer iterations across threads, then applies vectorization to the inner tiled loops.

transformations.name: Loop Unrolling
transformations.description: Replicate the loop body multiple times within each iteration to expose independent operations for instruction-level parallelism and reduce loop overhead.
transformations.rationale: After vectorization, the inner loop may still be latency-bound on FMA pipeline depth (typically 4-5 cycles on Broadwell). Unrolling by a small factor (2-8) exposes multiple independent FMA chains, enabling the out-of-order engine to overlap their execution and approach peak throughput. It also reduces branch overhead for tight loops.
transformations.action_template: LoopUnrolling(loop_id, unroll_factor) — unroll_factor specifies how many copies of the loop body to emit per iteration. loop_id identifies the target loop. OR LoopUnrolling(unroll_factor) — applies to the innermost loop by default.

intents.name: Iteration Space Restructuring and Work Distribution
intents.description: Restructure the computation into simpler forms and distribute work across multiple cores to exploit the available 28-core topology.
intents.rationale: The 7-dimensional convolution loop nest has a complex structure with kernel spatial reduction loops that can be simplified via lowering. Additionally, with 28 physical cores across 2 NUMA nodes, parallelizing outer loop dimensions provides significant throughput scaling. Im2col lowering converts the convolution to a matmul-like contraction that is more amenable to standard optimization patterns, while parallelization distributes the abundant outer-loop parallelism.

transformations.name: Im2col Lowering
transformations.description: Transform the convolution into a contraction (matmul-like) operation by explicitly materializing input patches, converting the kernel spatial reduction into a single matrix dimension.
transformations.rationale: Im2col eliminates the complex kernel-spatial reduction loops (KH, KW) by materializing the input patches as rows of a matrix, converting the convolution into a standard contraction. The resulting simpler loop nest is more amenable to tiling, vectorization, and other standard optimizations. This is particularly beneficial for non-1x1 kernels where the spatial reduction creates complex, strided access patterns that are difficult to optimize directly.
transformations.action_template: Im2colLowering() — no parameters; transforms the convolution operation into a contraction surrounded by reshape operations. Subsequent optimizations target the resulting contraction, not the reshapes.

transformations.name: Parallelization (Tiling-Based)
transformations.description: Partition the iteration space into coarse tiles and distribute them across threads for parallel execution.
transformations.rationale: Tiling-based parallelization provides flexible work partitioning that adapts to the varied shapes in this benchmark set. The RL agent can tune tile sizes to balance load across 28 cores while keeping per-thread working sets NUMA-local. This is the preferred approach when iteration counts along the target dimension do not divide evenly by the thread count.
transformations.action_template: ParallelizationTiling(tile_sizes) — tile_sizes specifies coarse tile dimensions for work distribution. The iteration space is partitioned into tiles of these sizes and tiles are distributed across available threads.

transformations.name: Parallelization (Thread-Count-Based)
transformations.description: Distribute loop iterations directly across a fixed number of threads without explicit tiling.
transformations.rationale: Direct thread-count-based distribution is simpler and avoids the overhead of explicit tile management. When outer loop iteration counts (e.g., batch size 128 or 256) are divisible by the thread count, this yields perfectly balanced work distribution. The common batch sizes in this benchmark set are powers of 2, making this approach well-suited.
transformations.action_template: ParallelizationThreads(num_threads) — distributes loop iterations across num_threads threads. num_threads must be a divisor of the iteration count to avoid remainder handling issues in subsequent MLIR lowering passes.
